But when Kendra stepped into the war room, badge swinging, hair still tied back in that Games-perfect braid, the air shifted. Addie didn’t flinch, didn’t falter — but Tier 1 saw it. He always saw it.

By noon, the room was hot with stale coffee and whiteboard dust. Addie started to push through lunch, flipping to the next page of her notes, when Tier 1’s hand clamped gently but firmly on her chair.

Tier 1 (low, to Addie):“Let’s grab food. Kendra and the team can run the numbers for an hour.”

Addie started to protest, but his look brooked no argument. He steered her out, down a side hall, through a glass door into the cool air of the courtyard.

They sat with plastic trays from the corner café, untouched sandwiches between them. Tier 1 leaned forward, forearms on the table, voice quiet but unwavering.

Tier 1:“Doc told me enough. Said I’m your guardian angel in the field. Nothing else, just that. The rest? I can see it myself.”

Addie stiffened, eyes on the bottled water in her hand.

That’s fine — I don’t need the details. What I need is this: how do I help? What blocks do I need to run between you two to make this project smoother?”

For a long moment, Addie said nothing. She just unwrapped her sandwich, staring at it like it was a code to be cracked. Then finally, she exhaled, shoulders slumping an inch — the closest thing to surrender Tier 1 had seen from her yet.

Addie (quiet):“Don’t let her see me crack. Not once. If she thinks I’m tired, cover it. If I need space, create it. If she pushes in too close… distract her. She deserves clean air. She deserves her lane.”

Tier 1 nodded slowly, as if memorizing a battle plan.

Tier 1:“Copy that. I’ll run interference where I can. You keep the mission upright. That’s our deal.”

Addie finally glanced at him, eyes rimmed but steady.

Addie:“Deal.”

Cole → team king (anchor for Addie’s survival).

Plot: Addie, Elena, and Kendra all need a breather → they fly down for a long weekend.

Scenes:

Late-night rooftop cocktails → Harper makes them each share one truth they haven’t said out loud yet.

Beach run at sunrise → symbolic of the “race” they’ve all been on, with Harper reminding them they don’t always have to sprint.

Grace + Lucas run around with Harper as the “fun aunt,” showing the next generation already being pulled into this Miami tradition.



3. Foundation Gala / Social Event (6–8 Months Later)

Plot: Harper hosts (or co-hosts with Addie’s Phoenix Foundation) a major charity gala in Miami.

Scenes:

Harper plays the elegant Miami hostess, showing she can shine socially just as much as she did operationally.

Addie + Hawk attend together as a couple, Chris + Kendra show up looking like stability incarnate.

Elena pulls Addie aside, teasing: “Remember when Harper couldn’t even sit still for one dinner? Look at her now.”

Harper admits later to Addie she sometimes misses “the game,” but this is where she’s meant to be.



4. Miami as the Refuge (1 Year Mark)

Plot: After a tough mission or personal breaking point (maybe post-Kendra Games pressure or Addie/Hawk conflict), Miami is where they retreat.

Scenes:

Harper has her doors wide open — literally leaves the gate unlocked because she knew they’d come.

A symbolic poolside scene → Addie floating, Hawk with Grace, Elena laughing with Kendra. Harper quietly observes: “This is why I stayed. To hold the center.”

Miami becomes the constant, balancing out Hawk’s intensity, Addie’s storms, and Kendra’s ambition.



🎯 Narrative Function of Miami

Harper = Anchor. Miami is the calm center of the wheel.

Setting contrast. While DC/NY/LA are work/missions, Miami is the heart retreat.

Family builder. Harper becomes the glue for the “sisterhood” and the kids, giving Grace & Lucas a playful, safe memory bank.

Arc resolution. By the time of Grace’s first communion, the Miami house is just as important as Jasper’s network or Addie’s apartment → a permanent safe haven.

Here’s a full chapter breakdown for Five Feet From Home with Jasper Barrett as a corporate crisis manager — showing his total immersion in the job while a family anchor keeps tugging at him.



Five Feet From Home — Chapter List

Part One — The Five-Foot World

(Jasper thrives inside his professional bubble, but cracks start to show.)

1. The Call — 2:17 a.m., London data breach. Jasper snaps into operational mode, assembling a team and flying out before dawn. First glimpse of the family anchor he leaves behind.

2. War Room — Jasper in his element: handling high-pressure executives, dictating media strategy, firefighting misinformation. Flashes of personal life only in the quiet in-between.

3. Passing Through — Brief stop at home between trips. He’s physically present but mentally elsewhere, already preparing for the next client emergency.

4. The Five-Foot Rule — We see how Jasper survives pressure: focusing only on what’s within immediate reach. Great for the job, destructive at home.



Part Two — Letting Both Teams Down

(He starts failing both at work and at home because his bubble is too small.)

5. Missed Flight Home — Chooses to stay an extra day in Hong Kong to secure a contract. Meanwhile, Grace (his daughter) has an asthma attack. Elena (his wife) leaves him a sharp voicemail he doesn’t answer.

6. A Slip in the Line — A junior associate mishandles a key client relationship because Jasper wasn’t watching the bigger picture. First time a colleague questions his leadership.

7. Our Team — At home, Grace asks if Daddy is “on our team.” Jasper freezes. The words stick in his head during the next crisis.

8. The Divide — Work colleagues notice Jasper’s distraction. Elena stops calling him when things break at home—she just handles them herself.



Part Three — The Reckoning

(Pressure forces him to look beyond the five feet.)

9. Rock Bottom — Chicago contamination case. Jasper arrives, executes flawlessly, but misses Grace’s recital—the one he promised to attend. Rookie consultant tells him, “You can’t manage a crisis if you’re living in one.”

10. The Offer — Global expansion role is on the table—his career peak, but a guaranteed death sentence for his home life.

11. Looking Up — Jasper chooses to turn down the expansion. Redefines success as mentoring and selectively taking cases that allow him to be home more.

12. Five Feet From Home — Jasper at Grace’s soccer game. Phone buzzes—a new crisis. This time, he turns it off. Final line mirrors title: “The world’s bigger than five feet, but it’s where I stand that matters.”
